title: File the annual unclaimed property holder report (New York)
description: Businesses holding property that has gone unclaimed — uncashed payroll or vendor checks, customer credits and refunds, unused gift cards, deposits — must report and turn it over to the state each year, after sending the owner a due diligence notice before the deadline. The annual report and payment are due March 10 for general property. The directory page defers to the Comptroller's calendar; March 10 comes from a 2026 industry guide, so confirm it. Which state's law applies depends on the owner's last known address, or the business's state of incorporation when there is none, so a business can owe reports to several states.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.

penalty.note: A holder that willfully fails to file a full report forfeits $100 for each day of delay, and late delivery carries interest (Abandoned Property Law section 1412); the Comptroller can waive part of the penalty.

title: Put freelance work of $800 or more in a written contract (New York)
authority: New York State Department of Labor
description: Under the Freelance Isn't Free Act (statewide since August 28, 2024), hiring a freelancer for $800 or more, counting all contracts with the same freelancer in the previous 120 days, requires a written contract with names and mailing addresses, an itemized list of services, the value, the rate and method of pay and the pay date. Keep it six years; the freelancer must be paid by the contract date or within 30 days of completing the work. Damages for failing to provide a contract on request start at $250 and can rise to the contract value.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee; this is a contracting requirement.

penalty.note: Damages start at $250 and can rise to the contract value.
